affiliations.research_notes: This is a military pathway, not a civilian employer. The indexed Sergeant classification is preserved even though both official histories document his later commission.

claims.temporal_assessment: The record dates Army entry but does not identify an OSS start, transfer sequence or employer.
claims.match_notes: Technician Fourth Grade is an enlisted grade and supports enlisted Army classification. It is not expanded to technical sergeant. The identifier remains private.

claims.claim_text: Raymond F Cooke's printed identifier lies inside a NARA-documented missing Army-file range, so the merged file's non-hit cannot resolve his identity or service.

claims.identity_match_assessment: No Army identity is assigned. The printed identifier supplies only a direct basis for explaining why the official merged file cannot answer the question.
claims.temporal_assessment: The range statement documents a source-coverage gap, not any employment or service chronology.
claims.match_notes: This is an archival-status claim only. It must not be read as negative proof or used to transfer facts from the different-identifier namesake.

claims.claim_text: Nick R. Kukich's best-supported immediate pre-OSS pathway was the United States Marine Corps, in which he was a sergeant at the point documented by OSS training and service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Marine Sergeant (and later lieutenant) Nick R. ("Cooky") Kukich
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS identifies Kukich as a Marine Sergeant who received OSS Area B and Area C training; the Marine history identifies the same man as Gunnery Sergeant and USMC radio operator on the November 1943 TANK mission.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The explicit NPS Cooky/Kukich correction and matching rank, service and mission details establish the person.
claims.temporal_assessment: His Marine Sergeant status is documented at OSS training and at the start of the November 1943 mission; the exact administrative accession date remains unknown.
claims.match_notes: The affiliation is a military assignment, not a civilian employer. His later second-lieutenant commission is documented but does not change the indexed Sergeant classification.
